description: Controlled vocabulary of classic errors. Each Challenge distractor may carry one code (server/src/data/qa/distractor-errors.json). Choosing a tagged distractor records the code on the attempt, which drives the 'Repeated mistakes' card and targeted drills.

TC_NO_2PI.title: Forgetting 2π in time constant ↔ LFF
TC_NO_2PI.tip: LFF = 1 / (2π × TC) and TC = 1 / (2π × LFF). Anchors: 1 s ↔ 0.16 Hz, 0.3 s ↔ 0.53 Hz, 0.1 s ↔ 1.6 Hz. Using 1/TC alone overstates the LFF about 6-fold.

TC_UNITS.title: Reading seconds as hertz (TC vs LFF)
TC_UNITS.tip: A time constant is in seconds; an LFF is in hertz. A 0.3-s time constant is not a 0.3-Hz filter: convert with LFF = 1 / (2π × TC).

TC_37_63.title: Mixing up 37% remaining with 63% lost
TC_37_63.tip: One time constant after a calibration step, about 37% of the deflection remains (63% has decayed). After two time constants about 13.5% remains.

CUTOFF_50_NOT_70.title: Using 50% instead of ~70% at a filter cutoff
CUTOFF_50_NOT_70.tip: At its cutoff frequency a filter passes about 70% of the amplitude (−3 dB), not 50%. Activity at the setting is reduced by about 30%.

FILTER_ALL_OR_NONE.title: Treating filters as on/off at the setting
FILTER_ALL_OR_NONE.tip: Filters roll off gradually: activity near the setting is partly attenuated, and some activity beyond the setting still passes. Nothing is cut cleanly at the number on the dial.

FILTER_DIRECTION.title: Confusing what the LFF and HFF act on
FILTER_DIRECTION.tip: The LFF (high-pass) attenuates SLOW activity and sets the decay of a calibration step; the HFF (low-pass) attenuates FAST activity and rounds sharp corners.

MASKING_A_FAULT.title: Hiding a technical fault with a filter or setting
MASKING_A_FAULT.tip: A notch, filter or sensitivity change hides the symptom but leaves the cause. Fix the electrode, impedance, ground or equipment first; document any filter you do use.

SENS_DIRECTION.title: Thinking a higher µV/mm makes waves bigger
SENS_DIRECTION.tip: Sensitivity is µV per mm. A larger number (e.g. 7 → 15 µV/mm) is LESS sensitive, so the same signal is drawn SMALLER.

SENS_ARITHMETIC.title: Dividing instead of multiplying with sensitivity
SENS_ARITHMETIC.tip: Amplitude (µV) = sensitivity (µV/mm) × deflection (mm). Deflection (mm) = amplitude ÷ sensitivity.

PAGE_SPEED_ASSUMED.title: Assuming 30 mm/s or a 10-s page
PAGE_SPEED_ASSUMED.tip: Always check the actual display speed or page width before measuring. At 15 mm/s a 30-mm span is 2 s, not 1 s, so frequencies would be doubled by mistake.

WAVES_NOT_PER_SECOND.title: Counting waves without dividing by time
WAVES_NOT_PER_SECOND.tip: Frequency = number of complete waves ÷ the time they span. Seven waves in 0.7 s is 10 Hz, not 7 Hz.

DECIMAL_SLIP.title: Decimal or unit-scale slip (×10, ms vs s, mV vs µV)
DECIMAL_SLIP.tip: Write units at every step: 1 mV = 1000 µV, 1 s = 1000 ms. A ×10 error usually means a lost unit conversion.

PEAK_TO_PEAK.title: Doubling or halving peak vs peak-to-peak
PEAK_TO_PEAK.tip: EEG amplitude is normally measured peak to peak. Do not double a peak-to-peak value or halve it unless the question asks for a peak value.

PERCENT_BASE.title: Percentage taken against the wrong base
PERCENT_BASE.tip: Percent change = difference ÷ the EXPECTED (reference) value. 8 mm against an expected 10 mm is 20% low, not 25%.

NYQUIST.title: Misapplying the Nyquist rule
NYQUIST.tip: Sample at more than twice the highest frequency of interest; the Nyquist frequency is half the sampling rate. Real anti-alias filters roll off gradually, so systems sample well above the minimum.

ALIASING.title: Misunderstanding aliasing
ALIASING.tip: Activity above the Nyquist frequency folds down to a false lower frequency and cannot be removed after sampling; only an analog anti-alias filter before digitisation prevents it.

TENTWENTY_MEASURE.title: Wrong 10-20 percentage or landmark
TENTWENTY_MEASURE.tip: Midline: Fpz 10%, Fz 30%, Cz 50%, Pz 70%, Oz 90% of nasion-inion. Coronal: T3 10%, C3 30%, Cz 50% of preauricular distance. Circumference: Fp1 5%, then 10% steps.

IMPEDANCE_LOGIC.title: Misjudging impedance or electrode behaviour
IMPEDANCE_LOGIC.tip: Balanced, low impedances let the differential amplifier reject common-mode noise; imbalance converts interference into signal. Mixed or polarizable metals cause drift.

CMRR_ALONE.title: Relying on CMRR despite impedance imbalance
CMRR_ALONE.tip: CMRR only rejects signals that arrive identically at both inputs. Unequal electrode impedances make 60-Hz interference differ between inputs, so it is amplified.

GROUND_REFERENCE_LOGIC.title: One-electrode vs whole-system fault logic
GROUND_REFERENCE_LOGIC.tip: A problem in one electrode appears in every channel containing that electrode; a problem in all channels of every montage points to the ground, reference or amplifier.

POLARITY_SIGN.title: Polarity convention or subtraction sign error
POLARITY_SIGN.tip: Channel = Input 1 − Input 2. If the result is negative the pen goes UP (negative-up convention). Work out each channel's sign before reading the picture.

BIPOLAR_ADDING.title: Adding instead of subtracting in a derivation
BIPOLAR_ADDING.tip: Every channel shows a DIFFERENCE between two inputs. −60 µV minus −100 µV is +40 µV, not 160 µV.

PHASE_REVERSAL_READ.title: Misreading a phase reversal
PHASE_REVERSAL_READ.tip: Pens pointing TOWARD each other mark a negative maximum at the shared electrode; pointing AWAY marks a positive one. Check polarity before naming the field.

END_OF_CHAIN.title: Missing an end-of-chain maximum
END_OF_CHAIN.tip: When the maximum is at the first or last electrode of a bipolar chain there is no phase reversal; confirm it with a referential or transverse montage.

REFERENCE_CONTAMINATION.title: Missing an active reference
REFERENCE_CONTAMINATION.tip: If every channel sharing one reference shows the same deflection, the reference itself (ear, Cz, average) is active. Re-reference before localising.

ISOPOTENTIAL.title: Reading a flat bipolar channel as 'no activity'
ISOPOTENTIAL.tip: A flat bipolar channel means the two electrodes are at EQUAL potential, which may be a field maximum or a salt bridge, not an absence of activity.

LOCALIZATION.title: Localising to the wrong electrode or region
LOCALIZATION.tip: Find the electrode common to the reversing pair, confirm in a second montage, and map the field before naming a lobe.

ARTIFACT_AS_CEREBRAL.title: Reading artifact as brain activity
ARTIFACT_AS_CEREBRAL.tip: Artifacts usually lack a physiological field, break the rules of polarity or appear in a single electrode, and often time-lock to ECG, movement or equipment.

CEREBRAL_AS_ARTIFACT.title: Dismissing brain activity as artifact
CEREBRAL_AS_ARTIFACT.tip: Activity with a plausible field across neighbouring electrodes, consistent polarity and evolution is cerebral until proven otherwise.

ARTIFACT_TYPE.title: Naming the wrong artifact source
ARTIFACT_TYPE.tip: Match the clue: time-locked to QRS = ECG; ~200-300 ms after QRS over an artery = pulse; F7/F8 opposite polarity = lateral eye movement; slow frontal with tongue = glossokinetic.

VARIANT_AS_ABNORMAL.title: Calling a benign variant abnormal
VARIANT_AS_ABNORMAL.tip: Wicket spikes, small sharp spikes, 14 & 6 positive spikes, rhythmic midtemporal theta, SREDA and mu are normal variants: no aftergoing slow wave, no field disruption, state-dependent.

ABNORMAL_AS_NORMAL.title: Missing an abnormality as a normal finding
ABNORMAL_AS_NORMAL.tip: Look for an aftergoing slow wave, field disruption of the background, asymmetry and persistence across states before accepting a pattern as normal.

AGE_NORMS.title: Wrong age-expected norm
AGE_NORMS.tip: Judge against age: PDR ~4 Hz at 4 months, ~6 Hz at 1 year, ~8 Hz by 3 years; tracé alternant disappears by ~44-46 weeks PMA; slower rhythms are normal in drowsy children.

SLEEP_RULES.title: Misapplying sleep staging or sleep graphoelements
SLEEP_RULES.tip: Stage by the majority of each 30-s epoch; N2 needs spindles or K-complexes; N3 needs ≥20% slow waves >75 µV; REM shows low tone with sawtooth waves and rapid eye movements.

ACNS_CRITERIA.title: Misapplying ACNS 2021 thresholds
ACNS_CRITERIA.tip: Seizure: >2.5 Hz for ≥10 s or definite evolution ≥10 s. BIRDs: >4 Hz, 0.5 to <10 s. IIC: PDs/SW 1-2.5 Hz. ESE: ≥10 continuous min or ≥20% of any hour.

ENCEPHALOPATHY.title: Misreading encephalopathy or coma patterns
ENCEPHALOPATHY.tip: Diffuse slowing, triphasic-morphology GPDs, FIRDA, alpha/theta/spindle coma and burst suppression are described by reactivity, continuity and frequency, not by a single feature.

ECI_REQUIREMENTS.title: Wrong ECI (brain death) recording requirement
ECI_REQUIREMENTS.tip: ACNS: full electrode set, ≥10 cm spacing, impedances 100-10,000 Ω, 2 µV/mm for ≥30 min, HFF ≥30 Hz, LFF ≤1 Hz, ECG, stimulation and an integrity test.

SYNDROME_MATCH.title: Wrong epilepsy syndrome for the picture
SYNDROME_MATCH.tip: Match age, seizure type and EEG together: 3-Hz spike-wave = absence; 4-6 Hz polyspike-wave = JME; hypsarrhythmia = infantile spasms; slow spike-wave + tonic = Lennox-Gastaut.

ACTIVATION_RESPONSE.title: Misreading an HV or photic response
ACTIVATION_RESPONSE.tip: Normal HV build-up resolves within about a minute; photomyogenic responses are frontal muscle time-locked to flashes and stop with eye opening; photoparoxysmal responses are cerebral spike-wave.

MEDICATION_EFFECT.title: Missing or misattributing a medication effect
MEDICATION_EFFECT.tip: Benzodiazepines and barbiturates increase frontocentral beta; reduced drug beta on one side suggests a lesion there. Sedatives also slow the background.

CONTRAINDICATION.title: Missing a contraindication or continuing an unsafe step
CONTRAINDICATION.tip: Screen before and stop during: recent stroke/TIA, sickle cell, significant cardiopulmonary disease or moyamoya limit HV; stop photic at a photoparoxysmal response; a sleep-deprived or sedated patient must not drive home.

PRIORITY_ORDER.title: Right actions in the wrong order
PRIORITY_ORDER.tip: Patient safety first, then preserve the evidence (test responsiveness, keep recording), then notify and document.

SCOPE.title: Acting outside technologist scope
SCOPE.tip: Technologists describe and document; physicians interpret, diagnose and order medications. Results are reported to patients by the interpreting physician.

UNDER_ESCALATION.title: Not escalating an urgent finding
UNDER_ESCALATION.tip: Seizures, status, ECI concerns and other critical findings are communicated promptly to the responsible physician with read-back, not left for the routine report.

PRIVACY.title: Confidentiality or HIPAA error
PRIVACY.tip: Use the minimum necessary information, share PHI only for treatment, payment or operations or with authorization, and route other requests through the privacy office.

CONSENT.title: Patient rights or consent error
CONSENT.tip: Patients (and guardians for minors, with the child's assent) may decline or withdraw at any time; explain, document and inform the physician. Use a qualified interpreter, not family, unless the patient specifically asks.

INFECTION_CONTROL.title: Wrong precaution or disinfection level
INFECTION_CONTROL.tip: Intact skin: low-level disinfection; non-intact skin: high-level; C. difficile: soap and water plus sporicidal cleaning; prion risk: disposable electrodes.

DOCUMENTATION.title: Improper documentation or correction
DOCUMENTATION.tip: Document objectively and at the time; correct with a single line, initials and date; annotate every setting change, event and medication on the recording.

EQUIPMENT_SAFETY.title: Wrong equipment, QA or electrical-safety decision
EQUIPMENT_SAFETY.tip: Remove failed or uninspected equipment from service, use a single patient ground, keep calibration logs and escalate validation failures to biomedical engineering.

ETHICS.title: Professional boundary or ethics error
ETHICS.tip: Avoid gifts that act as cash, conflicts of interest and dual relationships; disclose errors honestly; treat every patient equitably.

EMERGENCY_STEP.title: Wrong first-aid or BLS step
EMERGENCY_STEP.tip: Seizure: time it, protect, turn to the side, nothing in the mouth; call for help at 5 minutes or with injury; cardiac arrest: CPR and AED immediately.
